foods.name: Paneer Kathi Roll

units.basis: INDB serving size (derived: per-serving kcal / per-100g kcal x 100)

foods.name: Dates Chutney (Khajoor Chutney)
foods.notes: The sweet chutney used on chaat. INDB recipe has no added sugar (dates only); street versions often add jaggery or sugar. INDB serving ('small bowl', ~264 g) is the recipe yield, so tbsp/tsp are used instead (estimated weights).
foods.image_prompt: Glossy dark brown dates chutney in a small steel katori with a spoon

foods.name: Garlic Chutney (Poondu)
foods.notes: This is the South Indian wet chutney (garlic, shallots, tamarind, dried red chilli, tempered in oil). It is NOT the dry red lahsun chutney used in vada pav and dabeli, which was not found in the allowed sources. INDB serving ('small bowl', ~79 g) is too large for one person; tbsp is estimated.
foods.image_prompt: Deep red South Indian garlic chutney in a small bowl with curry leaves on top

foods.name: Schezwan Chutney
foods.notes: Homemade Indo-Chinese chutney (garlic, ginger, dried chillies, oil, soy, tomato sauce). Bottled brands differ; use their labels when available. INDB serving ('box', 1,553.26 kcal) is the whole jar, so tbsp is estimated. Macro check passes (+5.3%).
foods.image_prompt: Bright red schezwan chutney in a small dip bowl next to momos

foods.name: Chicken Biryani

units.label: 1 cup
units.basis: USDA portion: FNDDS 27243100 'Biryani with chicken', 1 cup = 196 g

source.ref: INDB ASC122 (Mutton biryani) recipe with chicken thigh (IFCT N002) for mutton; cooked weight by dry-matter balance (USDA SR Legacy water)

ingredients.name: Rice, parboiled, milled (100 g raw → 304.1 g cooked)
Chicken thigh, skinless, boneless (replaces INDB's 100 g boneless mutton; 100 g raw → 73.9 g cooked)
Oil (4 tbsp, as in the original recipe)

recipe.cooked_weight_basis: dry-matter balance with USDA SR Legacy water contents: rice parboiled dry 9.86 % (fdcId 169707) → cooked 70.36 % (169708), ×3.041; chicken meat raw 75.46 % (171052) → stewed 66.81 % (171451), ×0.739; onion raw 89.11 % (170000) → cooked 87.86 % (170001), ×0.897; tomato raw 94.52 % (170457) → cooked 94.34 % (170050), ×0.968; everything else at its raw weight
recipe.method: INDB ASC122 dum biryani: rice cooked with whole spices, layered with chicken cooked in onion-tomato-curd masala, saffron milk, sealed and steamed

foods.notes: Built from INDB's own recipe for mutton biryani (ASC122, 2 servings: 100 g rice, 100 g boneless meat) with chicken thigh in place of mutton. INDB publishes per 100 g of RAW ingredients (INDB.do: total nutrients / raw weight, no cooking water), so its 191 kcal/100 g is denser than biryani on the plate; here the cooked weight comes from USDA water contents. Oil: the original recipe says 4 tbsp (54 g); INDB's processed file has 4 tsp, which looks like a transcription slip. Bay leaf, saffron, chilli powder and cinnamon (~2.6 g, INDB's UK codes) and salt are left out (~5 kcal). IFCT chicken leg (N001) is not used: its energy contradicts its own macros. Restaurant biryani often has more ghee and more meat. Cross-check: a lab analysis of Hyderabad chicken biryani (Journal of Meat Science 2019, doi:10.5958/2581-6616.2019.00006.9) reports 434.7 kcal, 18.3 g fat and 16.5 g protein per 100 g on DRY weight; at 55–60 % moisture that is ~175–195 kcal per 100 g as eaten.
